requestedIntent: Owner decision 2026-10-27: detect recurring waste during the day (stuck agents, waiting work, idle or contended runners, review loops, forgotten sessions, inactive improvements, open work far past its expected time) in the coordinator's 15-minute check, turn breaches into owned alerts with deadlines in the central store, write real losses to the central log, and prepare a weekly retro the owner decides by number.

docs: CHANGELOG.md#Unreleased — Waste detection and weekly retro (2026-10-27)
CHANGELOG.md#Unreleased — acef-detect speed and stale acks (2026-10-27)

limitations: Wired, not enforced: nothing runs acef-detect on its own; the coordinator's 15-minute check has to call it, and nothing blocks an owner who leaves alerts unanswered (they become ALERT OVERDUE and go to the retro).
Resolution needs a positive observation: an alert whose subject vanished or aged out of every window stays open (printed UNSEEN) until the owner resolves it with evidence.
A source that keeps failing keeps its detector's alerts from resolving (SOURCE_ERROR every poll) until the source is repaired; this is deliberate.

Each detector needs host sources; an unconfigured one prints SKIP. On the first host the machine detector has no local slot event log (runner slots live on the runners), and no review report carries a finding-class field, so the review_loop class rule has no data.
Durations are wall clock from git timestamps and file times (nights and weekends included); cycle-time starts are unknown when a branch began before the history window.
Tests (slow or flaky suites) are not covered in this first version.

The run-item index trusts a file whose mtime_ns and size are unchanged; a rewrite that keeps both (for example a restored backup with its old times) is served from the index until the next change. Running items are never indexed. Deleting alerts/<project>.index.json or --no-cache forces fresh reads.

Stale acks need a breach observation: acks made before this version carry no breach record and become stale only after a later poll still sees them breaching after the recheck time; an acked alert that is only UNSEEN is never marked stale (the weekly retro still lists it as acked and open).

evidence.note: 2026-10-27: 151 checks passed, including review r1 regressions (no bytecode in the host or under a pycache prefix, 8 parallel polls open each key once, deferral deadline from expiry, aged-out or vanished runs not counted as recovered, missing tree hash is unknown, loss logged once when an open alert crosses 30 min); each regression failed on the pre-fix code. Review r2: per-detector tests that aged-out evidence stays UNSEEN and only a positive observation clears (stuck_agent command rule, review_loop rounds and class, machine hog, forgotten_session slot and worktree, size_ratio); the parallel-poll test holds the lock behind an lsof barrier and asserts every exit code. Review r3: git ancestry exit 128 and missing start stamps or attempt logs stay UNSEEN; exit 1, an observed finish or a produced result clears. Review r4: read contract — failing-source injection into every detector (SOURCE_ERROR, nothing resolves), ps exit 1, failed worktree listing, rc missing/null/empty, corrupt alert-log line; 18 of these checks fail on cb550d3. Review r5: unreadable glob subtree, rc false/0.5, invalid activation date, unreadable or undecodable alert log (exit 4), leftover with a removed parent; 8 of these checks fail on 602e48f.

2026-10-27: 45 checks passed: sections, numbers by route class with median or fallback, repeats with example and covering rule, overdue and unowned alerts, rules past review, at most five proposals, owner answers, no overwrite, RETRO DUE. A past week's snapshot ignores later events. An event exactly at the window's end belongs to the next week.
